IncidentCategoryCustomerFriendlyDescript: We regularly inspect trees near overhead power lines to keep your electricity supply safe and reliable. A recent inspection found some trees have grown too close to power lines. If unmanaged, branches could touch the overhead lines and cause unexpected interruptions to your electricity supply. We appreciate some customers may have experienced unplanned power cuts in the last 6 months. We need to trim these trees, which requires a temporary power cut because the work cannot be done safely while electricity lines are live. Due to the amount of work required we will need to switch off your power for a longer period. This work is taking place on a Saturday to minimise the impact to affected customers. This essential work involves approximately 450 metres of tree cutting across 8 sections of the overhead electricity network. This work is taking place near Chain Road.

Steps.Message: Hi, I'm Ebony and I am the manager of the text messaging team at UK Power Networks in Ipswich. Today's power cut was unexpected, so we were unable to provide you with prior notice to help you plan ahead. I am pleased to confirm that we managed to resolve this by repairing a faulty underground cable to get your lights back on as soon as possible. Just so you know, we text customers when we are made aware of problems like this, so if you would like to be notified in the future you can do so here https://UKPN.short.gy/SMS This was a widespread problem on the underground network and I personally apologise for any disruption this has caused to your day. If you have any questions or are still without power, please call us on 105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Maisy at 09:46 - I'm pleased to confirm that all power in the Odessa Road, E7 9 area should be back on. The issue was caused by an unexpected underground network fault, which our engineers have now repaired.

We know that a power cut can be difficult, and I'm sorry for the length of the time you were without your electricity. Please rest assured that our staff will continue to work around the clock to keep the lights on.

If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Sent by Bev at 12:16 - Our engineers have restored power to all 274 properties in the Beccles area, and we're pleased that this is sooner than we estimated. They have diverted power around an underground cable fault.

We know some properties in the area may have faced other recent interruptions, and we're sorry for the extra disruption. Every outage is fully investigated by our engineers, though power may be lost several times before we can safely find and fix the issue. Our customer services team will keep as many customers updated as possible during these investigations. 

We're sorry for the unplanned disruption. If you need to talk to us, or let us know that your power isn't restored, call us on 08003163105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
What will happen next?

This outage is affecting multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you'd expect. We have already sent staff to the area, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting the electricity around the faulty section. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to restore as much power as we can.

The engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will locate and repair the issue, which will take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team
